headline: PM Tarique Rahman discusses gas exploration with Chevron
summary: A high-level Chevron delegation met with the Prime Minister to discuss increasing investment in existing gas fields and exploring new reserves in Bangladesh.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with a high-level Chevron delegation today at his office in the Secretariat to discuss the country's energy sector.
The delegation was led by Javier La Rosa, president of Chevron Corporation’s Base Assets and Emerging Countries Division.
Key discussions focused on increasing Chevron's investment in both existing and older gas fields to optimize production.
The two sides also explored the possibility of exploring new gas reserves to ensure long-term energy security for Bangladesh.
The meeting was attended by Finance and Planning Adviser Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir and State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit.
Chevron Bangladesh President and Managing Director Shu Xiong and other senior officials were also present during the talks.
caption:
Bangladesh is looking to boost its gas reserves. PM Tarique Rahman and Chevron officials have met to discuss new investments.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with a high-level Chevron delegation today at his office in the Secretariat to discuss the country's energy sector.

The delegation was led by Javier La Rosa, president of Chevron Corporation’s Base Assets and Emerging Countries Division.

Key discussions focused on increasing Chevron's investment in both existing and older gas fields to optimize production.

The two sides also explored the possibility of exploring new gas reserves to ensure long-term energy security for Bangladesh.

The meeting was attended by Finance and Planning Adviser Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir and State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit.

Chevron Bangladesh President and Managing Director Shu Xiong and other senior officials were also present during the talks.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[launches 3-month dengue prevention campaign]]
headline: PM Tarique Rahman launches 3-month dengue prevention campaign
summary: The Prime Minister called for collective efforts to keep surroundings clean and eliminate mosquito breeding grounds to significantly reduce the disease.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has inaugurated the three-month nationwide "Dengue Prevention and Cleanliness Campaign-2026" at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban.
The Prime Minister urged citizens to spend just one hour every week cleaning their homes, workplaces, and study areas to ensure a quick success in tackling the disease.
He emphasized that preventing mosquito breeding is the safest and easiest way to fight dengue, warning that discarded plastic, paper, and other waste often collect stagnant water.
Tarique Rahman called for the active participation of millions of youth, including 2.5 crore students, 23 lakh Scouts, and 22,000 BNCC members, to help rebuild the country.
The Prime Minister also highlighted the role of the youth in bringing about change, referring to the mass upsurge on August 5, 2024, and urged them to now work together for a cleaner Bangladesh.
caption:
One hour of cleaning per week could save lives. PM Tarique Rahman launches a nationwide campaign to wipe out dengue.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has inaugurated the three-month nationwide "Dengue Prevention and Cleanliness Campaign-2026" at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban.

The Prime Minister urged citizens to spend just one hour every week cleaning their homes, workplaces, and study areas to ensure a quick success in tackling the disease.

He emphasized that preventing mosquito breeding is the safest and easiest way to fight dengue, warning that discarded plastic, paper, and other waste often collect stagnant water.

Tarique Rahman called for the active participation of millions of youth, including 2.5 crore students, 23 lakh Scouts, and 22,000 BNCC members, to help rebuild the country.

The Prime Minister also highlighted the role of the youth in bringing about change, referring to the mass upsurge on August 5, 2024, and urged them to now work together for a cleaner Bangladesh.
